ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$3.95 to the rider via Ryde voucher as partial refund of the metered distance fare for the unexplained off-route segment (14:27:55–14:33:25), and record the driver's breach of the shortest-and-most-direct-route obligation. No account flag (no prior upheld route dispute).

segment_findings.reason: Driver left the optimal route at ~14:27:25 and turned back at 14:28:25; the chat announcing the West Coast Highway route only came at 14:29:20 and the rider's consent at 14:30:00, i.e. after the segment started (RD-5: consent must precede the segment). Not exempt, but its net extra distance falls within the <0.2 km map-matching noise parameter used by the fact tool (implementation parameter, not a policy threshold under RD-1/RD-2).

Western routing 14:28:55–14:31:00 corresponds to the West Coast Highway change the driver raised at 14:29:20 and the rider explicitly agreed to at 14:30:00; agreement covers this segment (RD-5). No refund for this segment.

North-east excursion 14:31:25–14:33:25 looping back to the same point (1.2993,103.7633) where the car already was at 14:30:25: no onward progress, on neither the quoted AYE route nor the agreed West Coast Highway corridor, so no RD-5 agreement. No traffic-incident fact on the replaced stretch, and speed bands present are 4 and 5 (not band 1/2), so RD-4 gives no exemption. Extra ~2.80 km × S$1.41/km = ~S$3.95 refundable (RD-2 metered branch).
